rewrite: Plastic pollution is one of the worst environmental problems we face. Pictures of beaches covered in bottles and bags make it easy to feel overwhelmed. But local efforts show that change is possible, and already happening. In January 2025 the coastal town of Pantai Mutiara Timur started a deposit scheme that pays Rp 200 for every returned bottle. Within twelve months the town recovered 4.6 million bottles, and volunteer beach cleanups collected 71 percent less plastic than the year before. In my opinion the scheme worked because it turned waste into small but reliable income for scavengers and schoolchildren. A regional regulation now requires that "all beverage sellers display the deposit value on the label." Critics say such programs are costly, yet the town's budget shows the scheme cost Rp 1.3 billion, less than it used to spend on waste hauling. Not every region will get the same results. Still, incentives, not slogans, are what change behavior for good.

LedgerLite is a lightweight bookkeeping library for small businesses. The Open Finance Collective in Yogyakarta built it, and version 1.0.0, the first stable release, came out on 30 June 2026. LedgerLite enforces double-entry accounting, so every transaction must balance to zero before it can be saved. That rule prevents the silent drift in balances that affected the spreadsheets many early adopters used before. The library supports Python 3.11 and above and has no external dependencies apart from SQLite. On a standard laptop it posts 50,000 journal entries in under 9 seconds. Install it with pip install ledgerlite and run examples/quickstart.py. Note that "all amounts must be stored as integers in the smallest currency unit" to avoid floating-point errors. Contributions are welcome; 27 contributors have worked on the codebase so far. See CONTRIBUTING.md for details. LedgerLite is released under the Apache 2.0 license.

FieldNotes is an offline-first mobile app for researchers who collect survey data in remote areas. It was first built for the Coral Reef Monitoring Network of Wakatobi Selatan, whose teams surveyed 64 dive sites in the 2025 field season. The app stores every form locally in an encrypted database and syncs automatically when a connection returns. Offline storage matters because most survey boats spend up to 9 hours a day without mobile signal. Before FieldNotes, paper forms had to be retyped at the station, and an internal review found a 6 percent transcription error rate. The current release, v2.4, runs on Android 10 or later and supports photo attachments up to 12 MB each. To build from source you need Flutter 3.22 and a Firebase project configured for the sync service. Contributors should note that "every schema change must include a migration script and a rollback." FieldNotes lets scientists spend their time on research instead of paperwork. Licensed under GPL-3.0.

Queuebird is a job queue for Node.js applications. Handling background tasks well matters for the user experience. Two engineers at the agency Studio Kelapa started Queuebird in 2025 after their email jobs kept vanishing during server restarts. To fix that, every job is written to Redis before acknowledgment, so a crash never loses queued work. It requires Node.js 18 or newer and Redis 7.0 or newer. In production at Studio Kelapa, Queuebird processes about 1.8 million jobs per day with a median latency of 42 milliseconds. Failed jobs are retried up to 5 times with exponential backoff, starting at 2 seconds. Install it with npm install queuebird and set the connection in the QUEUEBIRD_REDIS_URL environment variable. The maintainers have one firm rule: "never merge a change that lowers test coverage below 90 percent." As of September 2026 the project has 3,400 stars on GitHub. We hope Queuebird helps you build faster, more reliable applications that scale.

Minutes of the Quarterly Board Meeting, Harbor Light Community Foundation. The meeting was held on Tuesday, 15 September 2026, at 2:00 p.m. in the foundation's main conference room in Bitung. Chairperson Grace Mandagi opened the meeting and welcomed attendees. Seven of nine board members were present, a quorum. The treasurer reported quarterly donations of Rp 412 million, an 18 percent increase over the previous quarter. The growth came mainly from the new monthly giving program, which has attracted 230 recurring donors since its June launch. The program director presented plans for a scholarship fund supporting 40 high school students from fishing families. After discussion, the board resolved that "scholarship recipients must maintain at least 85 percent school attendance." The board also approved a first-year budget of Rp 96 million for the scholarship program. Several members stressed transparent reporting to donors. The meeting was adjourned at 4:05 p.m.

Minutes: Engineering Sync, Project Kestrel, 23 September 2026. Attendees: Lina Hutapea (chair), Marco Siregar, Priya Nair, Joko Santoso, Ayu Lestari. Each member gave a short update. Marco reported that the payment service migration is 70 percent complete, with 11 of 16 endpoints moved to the new cluster. The remaining endpoints are blocked because the legacy database still uses a character encoding the new drivers cannot read. Priya noted that this blocker has already pushed the target date from 30 September to 14 October. Joko raised concerns about on-call load: 23 pages last week, most triggered by a noisy disk-usage alert. The team agreed to raise that alert threshold from 75 percent to 85 percent, effective immediately. Lina reminded everyone of the policy that "no migration step runs on Fridays or before public holidays." Action items were assigned; Ayu owns the encoding fix.

Minutes of the Residents' Association Meeting, Griya Permata Indah Block C. The meeting took place on Sunday evening, 20 September 2026, at the community hall, with 38 households represented. The association chair, Mr. Rudy Tanujaya, opened the session and thanked residents for taking part. The first item was security, after three motorbike thefts were reported in August. Residents agreed the thefts were likely enabled by the broken rear gate, which had been left open since its hinge failed in July. The meeting decided to repair the gate and install two CCTV cameras for a combined Rp 8.7 million. To fund this, each household will pay Rp 150,000 by 5 October 2026. The second item was waste collection, which the contractor has cut from three to two times per week. Residents resolved that "the contract will not be renewed unless collection returns to three times weekly."
